Article 6(c) prohibits inflicting on the group conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction in whole or in part. Track 2 applicants are disproportionately poor, female, and offered minimal housing or income support before approval for death.
The documentary stage below stitches the ACT IV chapter film. Then walk the evidence scene-by-scene. Atmosphere is not the proof; primary sources are.
Poverty share, female skew, material-resources and housing quintiles, palliative access gap.
About one in three Track 2 recipients reviewed reported poverty as a contributing factor. Housing and income offers were minimal or absent.
Ontario Track 2 skews female, poor, and isolated — clinical isolation, not an immigration chart. Housing crisis and gendered poverty on the coroner record.
Lowest material-resources and highest residential-instability quintiles — MDRC Marginalization Data Perspectives. Ledger atmosphere for deprivation, not a MAID volume chart.
Fewer than three in ten who could benefit receive palliative care — hospital corridor for care denied, set against rising MAID volume in the federal reports.
Film is memorial tone. Article 6(c) is argued from MDRC vulnerability and marginalization data , housing and poverty shares , and palliative access set against rising MAID volume.
